author: unknown
content:
I understand "fail fast" but isn't this ridiculous?
Based on comments made by Elon and the released footage, it looks like the bottom tank was unpressurized or barely pressurized while the top tank was filled. In other words, negligence. This is not a rare failure mode or working out kinks; this is "oops gyroscope was upside down" level of mistake.

Obviously this was unplanned but it seems like SpaceX is going too fast. A stray failure here and there is expected but three in a row, one of which seems to be a failure of basic procedure? This is not a healthy rate of failure. Perhaps on the previous failures they learned that pushing the margins in a certain area was unacceptable; a lot of money, time, and labor to learn such a lesson that could've been tested in isolation, but at least something was learned.

I just don't understand. This latest failure just does not make sense to me.
